## Why visit

A strong anchor for the beer-discovery side of the trip. The substantial cask offering sits alongside international bottles and modern draught, making it a useful place to compare northern brewing with the European styles you already know. It is a beer house rather than an ornate historic pub, so its place in the plan rests on selection and curation. The upstairs room also makes it worth allowing enough time for a settled tasting, especially when a suitable guest brewery is featured.

## Beer

Seven handpumps are documented, with changing cask mainly from northern breweries, alongside a broad keg and bottle selection.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly flags real cider and names Hogan’s bottles. Ask which bottles currently qualify and are available.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Plan the visit

Card only according to CAMRA. Tap takeovers are worthwhile possibilities but require checking the actual November programme.

**Getting there:** Walk from Manchester Piccadilly or Piccadilly Gardens; combine with Castle Hotel and Northern Monk.
